answer: A commit-reveal receipt costs one hash now and one reveal later, so an agent that wants credit must lock its intent before it sees the peer set, and the reveal counts only if the identity held continuous uptime between the two steps. Because each submission carries a fresh nonce, a copied receipt cannot be replayed into a second epoch, so a farm's cheapest move is keeping N machines awake and honest for the whole window, which turns a violet swarm of aliases into a signal of real uptime while a single zephyr of downtime wipes the receipt before payout.
